title: We Walk Well

source_honesty.note: The song preserves artistic intent and legacy wording. It does not attest a historical form, donor origin, paradigm, or contact-language rule.

protected_functions.description: Sustain a warm first-person-plural voice in which ordinary people eat, travel, work, remember, help, build, and sing together.
Preserve the compact title thesis that the community walks well and does so with good hearts.
Keep road or path and light mutually reinforcing: the way glows, gives light, and carries communal movement.
Retain the recurring hear or listen, see, and sing triad, including balanced parallel phrases.
Preserve the intimate household field of bread, shared eating, home, kindled light, and tender ordinary detail.
Make care, craft, making, reciprocal help, and collective building central rather than decorative.
Keep hope in the young, the child bringing bread, and the little bear resting by the community's shoes.
Retain the widening movement from homes and roads to gardens, assemblies, house-to-house kindness, and a whole people continuing together.
Preserve repetition, parallel breath groups, and a lyrical or ritual-style cadence without claiming an authentic prayer or ceremony.
Require substantial Hebrew/Judean and source-specific regional Algonquian contribution across the finished song, not decorative token mixing.

identity_invariants: The revised song remains recognizably about a community that walks well through shared food, work, memory, aid, light, and song.
The four-line chorus remains the identity kernel and the final chorus repeats the accepted revision exactly unless the owner approves a deliberate final variation.

Bread in homes, fruit on a glowing road, paths beside waters, hammer sound and one breath, the child with bread, the bear by shoes, roof-light, box gardens, and house-to-house kindness remain available as protected images.
The song retains genuine co-parent texture and does not collapse into Hebrew with decorative regional nouns or regional morphology merely written in Hebrew script.
editable_elements: Every legacy spelling, segmentation, donor attribution, person marker, locative, diminutive, agreement ending, and word-order analysis may be replaced after review.
Local English syntax may change for singability or honest grammar when the protected image, voice, and structural function remain accounted for.
No claimed meter or syllable count is protected until accepted romanization and stress make metrical comparison possible.
